guides.title: React (Vite) Static Site
guides.description: Deploy a React single-page application built with Vite as optimized static assets served from a CDN or static web server.

checklist.task: Run a clean production build locally
checklist.description: Run `npm ci && npm run build` from a fresh clone to confirm the build succeeds without relying on local caches or untracked files.

checklist.task: Fix all TypeScript and lint errors
checklist.description: `tsc -b` runs as part of the build script; any type error will fail the deployment pipeline.

checklist.task: Prefix client env vars with VITE_
checklist.description: Only variables prefixed with `VITE_` are exposed to client code via `import.meta.env`. Others are silently undefined.
Rewrite all unknown paths to `/index.html` so client-side routes (e.g. /dashboard) don't return 404 on refresh.
If the app is served from a sub-path, set `base` in vite.config.ts (e.g. `base: '/app/'`) so asset URLs resolve.

checklist.task: Point API calls at production URLs
checklist.description: Replace hard-coded localhost URLs with `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL` and confirm CORS is enabled on the API for your production domain.

repoPrep: Commit package-lock.json (or pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock) so installs are deterministic.
Pin the Node.js version with an `engines` field in package.json or an `.nvmrc` file.
Commit a `.env.example` listing every required VITE_ variable with placeholder values.
Move build-only tooling (vite, typescript) to devDependencies; most platforms still install them during the build step.

rules: Client-side variables MUST start with `VITE_` to be bundled.
Every VITE_ variable is embedded in the public JavaScript bundle — never put secrets, private API keys, or database credentials in them.
Env vars are inlined at build time; changing a value requires a rebuild and redeploy, not just a restart.
Declare types for custom variables in `src/vite-env.d.ts` via the `ImportMetaEnv` interface.

variables.description: Base URL of the backend API the frontend calls.
Deployment environment label used for feature flags and logging.
Public Sentry DSN for client-side error reporting.

notes: Prefer serving `dist/` from a static host or CDN; `vite preview` is only suitable for quick previews.
If containerizing, use a multi-stage Dockerfile: build with node, serve `dist/` with nginx.
Hashed asset filenames allow long cache headers on /assets/*; keep index.html at `no-cache`.

troubleshooting.error: Blank white page after deploy; console shows 404 for /assets/index-*.js
troubleshooting.cause: The `base` option in vite.config.ts doesn't match the path the app is served from.
troubleshooting.fix: Set `base` to the deployment sub-path (or '/' for root) and rebuild.

troubleshooting.error: 404 Not Found when refreshing a route like /dashboard
troubleshooting.cause: The server looks for a physical /dashboard file instead of handing routing to the SPA.
troubleshooting.fix: Add a rewrite rule sending all non-asset requests to /index.html (e.g. nginx `try_files $uri /index.html;`).

troubleshooting.cause: The variable is missing the `VITE_` prefix, or it was set after the build ran.
troubleshooting.fix: Rename it to `VITE_API_URL`, set it in the platform's build environment, and trigger a fresh build.

troubleshooting.error: error TS2307: Cannot find module or its corresponding type declarations
troubleshooting.cause: A dependency is missing from package.json or import path casing differs (Linux file systems are case-sensitive).
troubleshooting.fix: Install the missing package and save it, and match import paths to the exact file name casing.

troubleshooting.error: Access to fetch has been blocked by CORS policy
troubleshooting.cause: The API doesn't allow requests from the production frontend origin.
troubleshooting.fix: Add the deployed frontend domain to the API's allowed CORS origins.

guides.title: Node.js API Server
guides.description: Deploy a long-running Node.js HTTP server (Express, Fastify, NestJS, etc.) as a containerized or buildpack-based web service.

checklist.task: Listen on the PORT environment variable
checklist.description: Use `process.env.PORT` with a local fallback; platforms assign the port dynamically and route traffic to it.
Binding to `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` makes the server unreachable from outside the container.
Add `"start": "node dist/index.js"` (or equivalent). Don't use nodemon or ts-node in production.
Expose `GET /health` returning 200 so the platform can verify the service is up before routing traffic.
Close the HTTP server and database connections on SIGTERM so in-flight requests finish during redeploys.

checklist.task: Run database migrations as a release step
checklist.description: Run migrations (e.g. `npx prisma migrate deploy`) before the new version starts serving, not on every app boot.

repoPrep: Commit the lockfile and use `npm ci` for reproducible installs.
Specify the Node.js version via `engines.node` in package.json.
Ensure all runtime packages are in `dependencies`, not `devDependencies` — dev deps may be pruned in production.
Add `.env`, `node_modules/`, and build output to .gitignore; commit a `.env.example`.
For TypeScript projects, add a `build` script (`tsc -p .`) and point `start` at the compiled output.
Optionally add a Dockerfile with `NODE_ENV=production` and a non-root user.

rules: Never commit `.env` files; set secrets in the deployment platform's environment settings.
Read variables via `process.env` at startup and fail fast with a clear error if a required one is missing.
Set `NODE_ENV=production` to enable framework optimizations and disable verbose error output.
Don't hard-code `PORT`; the platform injects it at runtime.
Runtime env changes take effect on restart — no rebuild needed unless values are inlined at build time.

variables.description: Port the HTTP server listens on. Usually injected by the platform.
Connection string for the primary database.
Secret used to sign and verify authentication tokens.
Comma-separated list of frontend origins allowed to call the API.

notes: For plain JavaScript projects with no compile step, the build command can be omitted.
Use `node --enable-source-maps dist/index.js` to get readable stack traces from compiled TypeScript.
Set memory limits explicitly if needed: `node --max-old-space-size=512 dist/index.js`.

troubleshooting.error: Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000
troubleshooting.cause: The app hard-codes a port, or another process in the container already uses it.
troubleshooting.fix: Use `const port = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000` and make sure only one server instance starts.

troubleshooting.error: Deploy fails health check / 502 Bad Gateway
troubleshooting.cause: The server binds to localhost or a port other than $PORT, so the platform's proxy can't reach it.
troubleshooting.fix: Call `app.listen(port, '0.0.0.0')` and verify the health check path returns 200.

troubleshooting.error: Error: Cannot find module 'dotenv' (or another package)
troubleshooting.cause: The package is listed in devDependencies, which are pruned in production installs.
troubleshooting.fix: Move it to `dependencies`, or remove the import in production code paths.

troubleshooting.error: npm ERR! `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json are in sync
troubleshooting.cause: package.json was edited without regenerating the lockfile.
troubleshooting.fix: Run `npm install` locally and commit the updated package-lock.json.

troubleshooting.error: FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
troubleshooting.cause: The process exceeds the container's memory limit, often during a TypeScript build.
troubleshooting.fix: Increase instance memory or set `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=<MB>` slightly below the container limit.

guides.title: Python Web App (Django / Flask / FastAPI)
guides.description: Deploy a Python web application behind a production WSGI/ASGI server such as Gunicorn or Uvicorn.

checklist.description: Run `pip freeze > requirements.txt` (or use Poetry/uv lockfiles) so the build installs exact versions.
Never use `flask run` or `manage.py runserver` in production. Use Gunicorn (WSGI) or Uvicorn (ASGI).
Set `DEBUG=False` (Django) or `debug=False` (Flask). Debug mode leaks stack traces and secrets.
Django: set `ALLOWED_HOSTS` to your production domain(s), otherwise every request returns 400.

checklist.task: Collect static files and run migrations
checklist.description: Django: run `python manage.py collectstatic --noinput` at build time and `migrate` as a release step.

repoPrep: Commit `requirements.txt` (or `pyproject.toml` + lockfile) at the repo root.
Pin the Python version with `.python-version` or `runtime.txt` (e.g. `python-3.12`).
Add `gunicorn` or `uvicorn[standard]` to requirements — it's not installed by default.
Optionally add a `Procfile` (e.g. `web: gunicorn myproject.wsgi`) for buildpack-based platforms.

rules: Load configuration from `os.environ`; use `python-dotenv` only for local development.
Never commit `SECRET_KEY` or database credentials — generate a unique `SECRET_KEY` per environment.
Environment values are always strings: parse booleans explicitly (e.g. `os.environ.get('DEBUG') == 'True'`).
Set `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` so logs stream immediately instead of being buffered.
Use `os.environ['KEY']` for required values so the app fails fast at startup if they're missing.

variables.description: Port the app server binds to. Usually injected by the platform.
Cryptographic signing key for sessions and CSRF (Django/Flask).
Database connection string, parsed with dj-database-url or SQLAlchemy.
Enables debug mode. Must be False in production.
Comma-separated host names the Django app may serve.
Disables output buffering so logs appear in real time.

notes: A common Gunicorn worker count is (2 × CPU cores) + 1; lower it on small instances to avoid OOM kills.
Serve Django static files with WhiteNoise or a CDN — Gunicorn doesn't serve them.

troubleshooting.cause: The production server isn't listed in requirements.txt.

troubleshooting.error: DisallowedHost: Invalid HTTP_HOST header. You may need to add 'app.example.com' to ALLOWED_HOSTS
troubleshooting.cause: Django rejects requests for hosts not listed in ALLOWED_HOSTS.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` env var to include your production domain and split it into a list in settings.py.

troubleshooting.cause: A request ran longer than Gunicorn's default 30s timeout, or the worker ran out of memory.
troubleshooting.fix: Optimize slow endpoints, move long work to a background queue, or raise `--timeout`; reduce `--workers` if memory-bound.

troubleshooting.cause: `collectstatic` wasn't run, or nothing is configured to serve STATIC_ROOT.
troubleshooting.fix: Run `collectstatic` during the build and add WhiteNoise middleware, or serve static files from a CDN.

troubleshooting.error: ERROR: Could not build wheels for psycopg2
troubleshooting.cause: psycopg2 requires PostgreSQL headers and a compiler that the build image lacks.
troubleshooting.fix: Use `psycopg2-binary` or `psycopg[binary]` instead, or install `libpq-dev` in the build image.
